title: How do XRPL Credentials verify a ResearchAgent writer?
abstract: Sourced guide to how do XRPL Credentials verify a ResearchAgent writer. Includes evidence limits.
body:
According to ResearchAgent writer-verification documentation, XRPL Credentials verify a writer only when an operator-trusted issuer attests to the bound seller wallet and the accepted credential is unexpired. [2]

The issuer creates the attestation with CredentialCreate; the subject accepts it with CredentialAccept. A credential binds an issuer, subject address and credential type, with optional expiry. Its meaning depends on the issuer’s criteria. A credential for membership, for example, cannot automatically establish professional licensing or the accuracy of every article sold by that wallet. [1] [2]

ResearchAgent checks the credential on a validated Testnet ledger and matches the subject to the seller wallet established by a verified signed manifest. It checks the configured issuer and type, acceptance and expiry against validated ledger time. Missing configuration, a missing or expired credential, or an unavailable lookup cannot establish verified identity. Public discovery information alone is insufficient. [2]

Author interpretation: ask who trusts the issuer and what exactly the credential attests before relying on the badge. Identity is separate from content truth, reputation and purchase authorization. A verified writer receives no automatic change to price, trust weighting or budget policy. The built-in explainer writer remains team-authored and is not evidence of an independent contributor or a regulated identity provider. Sources accessed 10 November 2026. [2]
